paper.title_en: On the subtleties of statistical isotropy in cosmic topology
paper.abstract_en: The cosmological principle assumes homogeneity and isotropy on the largest scales for which the cosmic microwave background (CMB) provides the best testing grounds. Here, an analysis of the statistical isotropy for the CMB in the case of the cubic 3-torus topology is presented. Since the statistical anisotropy in the CMB 3-torus sky maps is very tiny, the analysis requires very large ensembles consisting of 100000 CMB simulations in order to reveal deviations from the isotropy. Orbit sum rules, which also have applications in quantum chaos, are used to describe the anisotropy structures found in the torus ensembles. They relate the length of orbits, which connect a given point on the surface of last scattering with the topological mirror points of the CMB observer, to the anisotropy pattern. It is found that the positions on the surface of last scattering which are closest to mirror observers possess the largest deviations from the statistical isotropy. Furthermore, the anisotropy of the normalised modulus of the gradient of the CMB temperature field is discussed.
